newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline firmer with strong U.S, but few ships.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline firmer with strong U.S, but few ships.

text.p: NWE gasoline was a touch firmer on Tuesday backed by good U.S demand, but activity was limited.
Traders said the U.S. arb was open but moving product transatlantic was hampered by a lack of shipping tonnage.
"It's more a matter of shipping than product avails," said one trader who said ships were scarce and freight rates strong.
Finding spot tonnage was difficult and any barrels moving transatlantic now would probably have to be carried in their own vessels or on time charter.
European demand was still quiet. A Eurograde barge was done at $224 fob and traders assessed cargoes at $223-227 cif NWE.
Ice problems were affecting business in ARA with empty barges travelling between Antwerp and Rotterdam in danger of being damaged.
In the Mediterranean a promptish 20,000 tonne Eurograde cargo was offered at around high fob +$1/+$2.
